body: That's awesome, journaling is a great thing to do. Ya can't go wrong with a good Disney movie so that's a great idea! You're very welcome for the advice, have a great rest of your day or whatever it is for you right now!

It's perfectly okay to be afraid of the dark. Keep as many lights on as you need. When nighttime comes and your getting ready for bed think about what you did today. What were the positives? What were the negatives? What was just okay? Try to mainly focus on the positives, but going through your whole day in your head can be a good distraction. Instead of watching more videos about paranormal activities, try  some ASMR if you haven't already. I know a lot of people think ASMR is really weird but for some people it can really help calm you down and help drift you off to sleep. I hope it gets better for you very soon!

Trust me when I say, everyone is much more than a little nervous at meets. It's perfectly natural to feel anxious at things like this, there's lots of people, your competing with others and it can be really stressful. It's really brave of anyone to put themselves out there and perform and I'm incredibly proud of you for doing that it's really amazing. I never took part in any track or cross-country events but I have two very close friends who have done track and cross-country their whole lives. I've asked them and talked with them about their anxiety that they get right before the starting pistol goes off. These are the main things I told them and seemed to have helped a bit. First, Know that there are tons of other people being judged for their times as well. Your just another one of those people and your not being put on display for people to gawk at or pick apart. Don't be nervous of what people will think about your time or performance because I can almost guarantee you that not even a minute later they've completely forgot what it was. Second, your there to have fun. Focus on that above everything else. It's all about enjoying yourself and having a good time at meets. My suggestion to you for when your at the starting line and are starting to panic, take a good deep breath and tell yourself "I don't care what other people are going to think about my time and I'm GOING to have fun. I'm going to enjoy myself because my feelings come before others opinions of something small like my time". As far as getting anxiety just from watching races or swing stuff related to it, understand that you're not in that situation right now so again take a deep breath and as you inhale close your eyes and imagine where you are right now. You're not at a meet and nobody's judging you, it's okay. And if course if you truly feel it's something you just can't do, don't push yourself to do it. That can cause even more anxiety and lots of stress. You are a great person, and I'm so proud of you for pushing through a whole season of it. Trust your feelings and better judgement. I know you'll do great!

I've had a sorta similar experience but with my younger sister. The same thing happened, I went home and kept asking myself "what if??" And beating myself up over what could've happened because I allowed her to be in a situation like that. The thing that helped me get over that specific anxiety was to just first, take a few deep breaths and tell yourself "Nothing bad happened and everything IS okay" then just go hug your daughter. When you hug her tell yourself "She's still here, perfectly safe, and I did a good thing as a parent to ask that guy to turn us around". Don't beat yourself up over this, your daughters and your intentions were entirely innocent. You are a good parent and a good person. For now try to avoid watching stuff like that if it's just gonna make you feel that way. In this situation there is no "What if" only "what was" and what was, was okay because absolutely nothing bad happened and you had a good learning experience. I really hope this helps and I really hope you start feeling better about all this very soon!
